text:
anya: Quick post-RFC follow-up — I sketched a small rollout playbook for per-model kernel enablement and graceful fallback. Wanted feedback before we file the checklist in the RFC repo.

julia: love the idea of a compact playbook. can we make the default behavior 'safe-fallback-to-cpu' + rapid rollback? :thumbsup:

samir: proposal notes: we need both policy and telemetry hooks. policy = flag hierarchy (org > team > model > variant). telemetry = latency P50/P95, error rate, token throughput, and hallucination regressions (eval prompts).

anya: Agreed. rough rollout steps I have: 1) feature flag off 2) enable on 1 model for internal traffic 3) canary to 5% prod with slow ramp 4) 25% 12h window 5) 100% if green. fallback rule: if latency P95 > baseline * 1.5 OR 5xx rate > 0.5% -> instant degrade to fallback kernel.

todd: Add a circuit-breaker on per-model queue depth too. If queue depth spikes, we should shed to cheaper kernels or deny-new-requests until backpressure clears.

maria: important: decide where flags live. I vote runtime flags in config-service (k8s CRD) + override via admin console for emergency rollback. Keep gating in the control plane, not in model binary.

samir: +1. also want to record the flag provenance for audits (who flipped, when, reason). ops-bot should log flips to #incidents automatically.

julia: small config example for the flag schema: 
```yaml
flag_name: kernel_chosen.alpha_attention_opt
scope:
  type: model
  id: gpt-xl-v2
rules:
  - condition: "user_org == 'internal'"
    rollout: 1.0
  - condition: "traffic_pct <= 5"
    rollout: 0.05
fallback: kernel.default.quantized
metrics:
  - latency_p95
  - error_rate_5xx
failure_action: degrade_to_fallback
```

anya: This is great. One open tradeoff: how granular are kernels allowed to be? per-model-version vs per-architecture. Too fine-grained = config explosion. I propose allowing per-model-version but defaulting to model-family buckets.

todd: Another ops detail: when we flip a kernel on, we should warm the KV cache; rollout must include a short warm window for cached weights. Otherwise first requests spike latency. Maybe pre-warm by fanout to a small set of nodes.

maria: Monitoring playbook: add synthetic prompts to catch quality regressions — we run eval set every 15 min against canary traffic and compare embeddings similarity + perplexity heuristics. If delta exceeds threshold -> rollback.

samir: For emergency fallback, define two levels: soft-fallback (route new requests to fallback kernel but let in-flight finish) and hard-fallback (kill canary workers and route everything away). Have an automated hard-fallback if 5xx > 1% for 5min.

ops-bot: deploy-lock engaged by anya at 1854321200 — rollout started for kernel_chosen.alpha_attention_opt on gpt-xl-v2 (canary 5%).

deploy-bot: canary snapshot created: snapshot-id:a5f3b2. rolling to 12 nodes.

julia: small UX ask: include 'expected regression risk' in the flag UI (low/medium/high) and a quick link to the eval-run for that model so PMs can review before broader rollout.

anya: next actions: (1) todd to add queue-depth circuit-breaker PR; (2) maria to wire synthetic eval checks into the alerting rule; (3) samir to add flag provenance logging. I'll draft the playbook doc from this thread and link to RFC. target: have checklist + config templates by EOD Fri.

todd: on it. PR by tomorrow.

maria: adding alerts today.

samir: will start audit logging work, tagging it 'post-rfc runtime rollout'.

anya: thanks all. Will ping again once the doc hits the RFC repo. :rocket:
